summary: Complete finite Poisson host/PTX execution and bind exact residual acceptance to its actual returned memory.

examined.reason: Close finite host composition using concrete kernel witnesses, physical layout projections and static-byte preservation; bind exact acceptance to initial problem and actual final solution words. Replace obsolete chronological gap descriptions with current self-contained contracts and exact proof links.
Describe complete finite modeled solver execution and accepted returned-memory certification, retaining full PTX and external hardware/transport boundaries.
Discrete Poisson equations, setup, numerical reference and accepted residual target are unchanged. Host composition implements the existing restricted backend responsibility.

Primitive semantics are unchanged. The new host proofs reuse existing necessary source constraints; differential mock tests are explicitly source-fidelity tests, not hardware verification. Exact dependency audits retain only standard Lean axioms.
No instruction or memory model is broadened. Publication composes completed recorded stores; full PTX memory admission and hardware visibility remain separate.

results.method: Sequential capped Lean module checks; complete exact dependency audit, source guards and pins; twelve emitted-PTX binding checks and a differential Python/Lean host-control check; frontend tests; manual concrete launch, physical-layout, byte-frame, input-preservation and exact acceptance review; Stratic validation and matching snapshots.
results.environment: Pinned Lean 4.34.0 and 16 dependency pins; one heavy process at a time, one Lean thread, 6 GiB cgroup, swap disabled, CPU quota 150 percent. No GPU runs or paid model calls.
results.evidence: All 26 new Lean modules check without warnings, adding 142 declarations. The exact audit passes 6602 dependency reports and 932 guarded sources with only standard Lean axioms; all 16 dependency pins pass. The concrete host launch relation covers all 21 runtime entries using actual fetched instructions, returns, necessary source admission and recorded publication. Physical layout and uploaded connectivity/assembly validity suffice to construct a finite complete host execution; the proof discharges local execution obligations rather than assuming total kernel launches. Actual write footprints preserve uploaded equations and table validity throughout the loop. Every completed execution obeys the 6+17*maxiter launch bound. The exact certificate decodes original problem words and actual final x words, proving zero boundary and the requested real residual bound on acceptance. Raw convergence does not imply certification. The actual Python host and Lean schedule agree on all 168 mock-kernel scenarios, including exceptional status, stopping precedence, periodic checks and final-iteration restart. All 77 frontend tests pass; a new negative test rejects mismatching uploaded boundary flags before serialized certification. All twelve PTX receipts refreshed; unchanged legacy executable reuse limited to verified import closures, with current audit and rendering checks rerun. README and emitted PTX unchanged. Stratic descriptions are consolidated around current contracts and exact implementation links; study guides describe the complete host proof. Full PTX memory admission, external serialization/transport, compiler/CUDA/GPU fidelity and scheduler fairness remain explicit external boundaries. No unconditional convergence, CPU bitwise equality or PDE error guarantee. The unchanged legacy interpreter suite was not rerun. Audit peak RSS 5123836 KiB.
